title: Regla 5: pronombres de objeto directo (lo, la, los, las)
source: Slide 20 and the songs No lo tengo / Guapo
summary: lo / la / los / las stand in for the thing that receives the action. They go before the verb.
instruction: Fill in the direct object pronoun
explanation: Rule 5: Direct object pronouns are pronouns that stand in for the direct object of a sentence. The direct object receives the action / attention of the verb.
¿Tienes el diccionario? = Do you have the dictionary? (the dictionary is the direct object). No, no lo tengo. = No, I do not have it. Here lo takes the place of diccionario. It's a D.O. pronoun.

Direct object pronouns must agree in gender and number with the nouns they replace: lo = it (masculine), la = it (feminine), los = them (masculine), las = them (feminine). Notice the pronoun goes before the verb: no lo tengo.
This is the whole point of the Señor Wooly song No lo tengo, and it shows up in Guapo too: ¿Personalidad? Él no la tiene.

examples.es: ¿Tienes el diccionario? No, no lo tengo.
examples.en: Do you have the dictionary? No, I do not have it.

examples.es: ¿Tiene José sus computadoras? Sí, las tiene.
examples.en: Does José have his computers? Yes, he has them.
